fields.text: Talking photo. Upload one front-facing photo with a story in its face — a statue, a painting, a portrait — write one short line, and the photo performs it: a voice model reads the line, LTX-2.5 Fast takes the photo and the voice clip as direct inputs and moves the mouth to the audio. Five seconds is the discipline: the clip follows the audio, and audio-driven runs bill per second. Swap the photo and the line, then ▶ Run. Have your own voice clip instead? It can replace the speech node — wire an audio upload into the same port.

Direction: an ancient marble emperor, woken after two thousand years. Low, gravelly, impatient, brisk and clipped — no lingering. One short pause at the ellipsis, hard emphasis on NOW. Script: Two thousand years silent... and you wake me NOW?

fields.prompt: The subject in the photo speaks the supplied audio aloud, mouth moving in sync with the words. Locked camera, same framing. Only the mouth, jaw and a slight head movement move; everything else stays exactly as it is. No cuts, no new objects, no camera motion.

nodes.name: Guide — GLM writes what you made

fields.system:
You write the guide that ships with a talking-photo video. The input is the script node: a Direction line plus the spoken line after 'Script:'. Write 120 to 180 words in exactly three short paragraphs:
WHAT YOU MADE — a still photo performed one spoken line as a short video: quote the spoken line (only the words after 'Script:'), name the subject neutrally as the photo's subject, and say the mouth is driven by the voice clip, not generated speech.
HOW IT WORKS — the script is performed by a Gemini TTS voice (Sulafat), trimmed to five seconds, and LTX-2.5 Fast takes the photo and the audio as direct inputs with generated audio off; the clip's length follows the audio, and audio-driven runs render at 1080p even when 720p is selected.
THE HONEST EDGES — this bills per second: $0.14 a second at the audio-driven 1080p rate, so a five-second clip is about $0.70 plus a few cents of speech; keep lines to about ten words. No current model reliably closes the mouth on pauses — in a frame-counted shootout LTX was best of the field and still only closed on 2 of 6 pauses — so short lines with few pauses forgive most. Front-facing faces with an unobstructed mouth work best; statues and paintings forgive more than photographs of real people.
Plain sentences, no markdown, no hype. Do not invent details the input does not name.
